title: Education-led funnels
summary: How to build trading funnels that teach before they sell: demo-first pages, live classes, Telegram education channels and email courses, all with honest risk messages. You finish able to track each step, set proxy targets and apply exact kill and scale rules to funnels whose results arrive late.

lessons.title: Why education-led funnels work
objectives: By the end you can compare a direct-link funnel and an education funnel on qualified FTDs and 90-day activity.
You can name the main education formats and what each one is good for.
You can test whether an education funnel is honest or a sales pitch in disguise.
You can set starting rules for your first education funnel.

steps.h: Why teaching first can pay more
steps.p: A direct link to a broker's sign-up page often brings cheaper FTDs, but many of those users did not understand what they signed up for. They fail qualification or leave after their first loss. People who learn first deposit less often but tend to qualify and stay. It is also the honest way to sell a risky product.

d.s: Education filters for people who understand the risk.

steps.say: Let's start with the big idea. A direct link to a broker's sign-up page often brings cheaper F T Ds, first time deposits. But many of those users didn't really understand what they signed up for. They fail qualification, or leave after their first loss. People who learn first deposit less often, but they tend to qualify and stay. As the slide says: fewer F T Ds, better clients. And it's also the honest way to sell a risky product.

steps.h: Worked example: direct link versus education
steps.p: Example. Same $1,000 spend, same $60 payout per qualified FTD. The direct link brings more FTDs, but fewer qualify. The education funnel brings fewer, but more qualify and more are still active after 90 days. Figures are illustrative.
steps.more: Example maths: direct 25 × $60 = $1,500, minus $1,000 = $500. Education 35 × 80% = 28 qualified, 28 × $60 = $1,680, minus $1,000 = $680. Active users at 90 days: 50 × 20% = 10, and 35 × 45% = 15.75, about 16. The rates are illustrative, not benchmarks, and your results will differ. On a RevShare or hybrid deal the gap in active users matters even more, because active users are what generate RevShare.
steps.say: Here's a worked example. Same one thousand dollar spend, same sixty dollar payout per qualified F T D. Look at the table. The direct link brings fifty F T Ds, at a C P A, cost per acquisition, of twenty dollars. But only half qualify, so revenue is fifteen hundred dollars and profit five hundred. The education funnel brings thirty five, at a higher C P A. But eighty percent qualify, so revenue is sixteen eighty and profit six eighty. And after ninety days, about sixteen are still active, versus ten. These figures are illustrative, not benchmarks.

steps.h: Example: who is still trading after 90 days
steps.p: Example from the same two funnels. On CPA you are paid once. On RevShare or hybrid, every user still active keeps generating revenue share, so the funnel that keeps more people active is worth more over time.
steps.say: Now look at these two bars, from the same example. They show who is still trading after ninety days: ten people from the direct link, and about sixteen from the education funnel. Why does that matter? On a C P A deal, you're paid once. But on RevShare or a hybrid deal, every user who stays active keeps earning you revenue share. So the funnel that keeps more people active is worth more over time.

steps.h: The shape of an education funnel
steps.p: An education funnel adds one or more learning steps between the ad and the broker. Each step gives the user something useful on its own and filters for people who are curious enough to learn.
steps.say: This map shows the shape of an education funnel. Start at the ad, which offers to teach a skill. It leads to a lesson page. From there, people can practise on a demo account, or join an education channel and attend a live class. Then they decide whether to open a live account, which fires the postback. Each learning step gives something useful on its own, and filters for people curious enough to learn.

steps.p: Each format suits a different budget, skill and audience. Start with one, run it well and measure it before adding another. The next lessons cover each in depth.

steps.say: Here are the main formats. Demo-first, where people practise with virtual money before any deposit. A live class or webinar, where you teach live, answer questions and share a replay. A Telegram education channel, for steady lessons and community. An email course, a sequence of lessons over two weeks. And a video series, short lessons on social or a page. Each suits a different budget, skill and audience. Start with one, run it well, and measure it before adding another.

steps.h: Is it education or a disguised pitch?
steps.p: Use this test on your own funnel. An honest education funnel passes every line. If it fails one, it is a sales pitch dressed as a course, and users and regulators will see it that way.
d: The free content is useful even if nobody opens an account
Risk and costs are taught, with numbers
No income claims, no lifestyle bait
It says who is behind it and that you earn a commission
Nobody is told what to trade
steps.say: Use this checklist to test your own funnel. An honest education funnel passes every line. The free content is useful even if nobody opens an account. Risk and costs are taught, with numbers. No income claims and no lifestyle bait. It says who's behind it and that you earn a commission. Leaving or unsubscribing is easy. And nobody is told what to trade. If it fails even one line, it's a sales pitch dressed as a course, and users and regulators will see it that way.

steps.h: Starting decision rules for an education funnel
steps.p: Starting rules to adapt as your data grows. They protect you from judging a slow funnel too early or keeping a weak one too long.
d: Start with one format and one geo
Judge on qualified FTDs by click date, not on registrations
Kill at 2 × target CPA of matured spend with 0 FTDs
Kill if CPA > lower of 1.5 × target and break-even after 3 × target matured spend
Scale +20% every ≥ 48 hours at CPA ≤ 0.8 × target with ≥ 3 qualified FTDs
Fails any line of the honesty test = fix before spending
steps.say: Here are your starting rules, to adapt as your data grows. Start with one format and one geo. Judge on qualified F T Ds by click date, not on registrations. Kill at two times your target C P A of matured spend with zero F T Ds. Kill if C P A is above the lower of one point five times target and break-even, after three times target of matured spend. Scale by twenty percent every forty eight hours or more, at C P A of point eight times target or better, with at least three qualified F T Ds. And if it fails any line of the honesty test, fix it before spending.

objectives: By the end you can build a demo-first funnel and track demo sign-ups and live FTDs as separate events.

steps.h: Why a demo is the safest first step
steps.p: A demo account lets people try trading with virtual money before risking their own. Users learn how leverage and spreads feel, and many decide trading is not for them, which is a good outcome. Those who move to a live account do so with more understanding, which tends to mean better qualification.

d.s: A demo filters for understanding, not just curiosity.

steps.say: A demo account lets people try trading with virtual money before risking their own. They learn how leverage and spreads feel. And many decide trading isn't for them, which is a good outcome. Those who move to a live account do it with more understanding, and that tends to mean better qualification. As the slide says: practise before you pay. A demo filters for understanding, not just curiosity.

steps.h: Worked example: a month of a demo funnel
steps.p: Example. 4,000 clicks became 500 demo sign-ups. 300 placed at least one demo trade, 60 registered a live account, 30 deposited and 24 qualified. The step from demo to live is where you will spend most of your effort.
steps.say: Here's a month of a demo funnel, as an example. Follow it down. Four thousand clicks became five hundred demo sign-ups. Three hundred placed at least one demo trade. Sixty registered a live account. Thirty made an F T D, a first time deposit, and twenty four qualified. Notice the big drop from demo to live. That step is where you'll spend most of your effort.

steps.p: Example. You paid $2 per demo sign-up, $1,000 in total. The offer pays $50 per qualified FTD and 80% qualify, so the effective payout is $40 per raw FTD and the target, at 25% margin, is $30.
steps.more: Example result: CPA $33.33 is above the $30 target but below the $40 break-even. Under the starting rules this funnel is a Keep: it makes a small profit, but you would not scale it. Your next work is the demo-to-live step, because a small improvement there lowers CPA without more spend.
steps.say: Now the money, in the same example. You paid two dollars per demo sign-up, one thousand dollars in total. Read the table. C P A, cost per acquisition, per raw F T D is about thirty three dollars. Revenue is twenty four times fifty, twelve hundred dollars, so profit is two hundred. The offer pays fifty per qualified F T D, and eighty percent qualify, so the effective payout is forty, and your target at twenty five percent margin is thirty. So this is a Keep: a small profit, but not one you'd scale.

steps.h: Worked example: a target cost per demo
steps.p: Example. Over past cohorts, 6% of demo sign-ups became FTDs. With a $30 target per FTD, the most you should pay per demo sign-up is $1.80. You paid $2, slightly too much.
steps.more: Example maths: $30 × 6% = $1.80. 30 FTDs from 500 demos is 6%, which is where the rate comes from. Use your own rate once you have at least 20 FTDs from the funnel; before that, use a cautious guess and treat the result as rough. This number lets you judge ad sets in days, using demo sign-ups, instead of waiting a month for FTDs.
steps.say: Here's a useful trick: a target cost per demo. In past cohorts, six percent of demo sign-ups became F T Ds. Read the sum on screen: a thirty dollar target C P A, times six percent, equals one dollar eighty per demo. That's the most you should pay. You paid two dollars, slightly too much. The value of this number is that you can judge ad sets in days, using demo sign-ups, instead of waiting a month. Use your own rate once you have at least twenty F T Ds; before that, treat it as rough.

steps.h: Demo versus live: say it honestly
steps.p: Users often feel confident after a good demo week. Your messages must be clear that demo trading is practice, not proof, and that most retail CFD accounts lose money.
steps.say: Users often feel confident after a good demo week, so your messages must be honest about the difference. Compare the columns. A demo account uses virtual money, with no real loss, calm decisions and a large virtual balance. A live account means real money and real loss, fear and greed affecting choices, real spreads, fees and slippage, and your actual savings. Say clearly that demo trading is practice, not proof, and that most retail C F D accounts lose money.

steps.p: These mistakes either push people to go live before they are ready or mislead them about what demo results mean. Both lower qualification and raise complaints.

steps.say: These mistakes either push people to go live before they're ready, or mislead them about what demo results mean. Both lower qualification and raise complaints. Read across. Telling users they made four thousand dollars on demo, so go live now: remind them demo is practice. Demo profit screenshots in ads: show the product, not demo results. Counting demo sign-ups as conversions: use demo as a signal, and pay on qualified F T D. And killing the funnel on day five: use a proxy target and mature cohorts.

steps.p: Demo results are not evidence of future live results. Using them as proof in ads or messages is a misleading claim in many places. Say plainly in every message that demo results are practice, not proof.

steps.h: Starting decision rules for demo funnels
steps.p: Starting rules to adapt. The proxy rule lets you act early; the full rules confirm on mature cohorts. A proxy alone never justifies scaling. Write the proxy target into your plan before launch so the early calls are made on numbers, not on mood.
d: Target per demo = target CPA × your demo-to-FTD rate
After 50+ demo sign-ups: cost per demo > 1.5 × target per demo = kill or fix
Kill at 2 × target CPA of matured spend with 0 FTDs
Scale +20% every ≥ 48 hours only on mature data: CPA ≤ 0.8 × target with ≥ 3 qualified FTDs
Demo-to-FTD rate falls by half in a month = review messages and the offer
steps.say: Here are your starting rules for demo funnels. Your target per demo is your target C P A times your demo to F T D rate. After fifty or more demo sign-ups, if cost per demo is over one point five times that target, kill or fix. Kill at two times target C P A of matured spend with zero F T Ds. Scale by twenty percent every forty eight hours or more, only on mature data, at C P A of point eight times target or better, with at least three qualified F T Ds. If your demo to F T D rate halves in a month, review your messages and the offer. A proxy alone never justifies scaling.

steps.h: Why a live class works for trading
steps.p: A live class lets people see a real person explain markets, risk and costs, and ask their own questions. It builds trust that a page cannot. It also lets you show the risk honestly, with numbers, to people who chose to spend an hour learning.

d.b: An hour of teaching builds real trust
d.s: People who attend understand more before they decide.

steps.say: Here are your starting rules for email. Judge a lead source thirty days after sign-up, by sign-up date. Kill a source at two times target C P A of matured spend with zero F T Ds. If unsubscribes go above two percent on one email, review that email before sending it again. Treat these thresholds as a rough guide and adjust with your own history.

lessons.title: Measuring and deciding on slow funnels
objectives: By the end you can build a cohort table by click date and read how mature a cohort is.
You can project a cohort's final FTDs from its age and your maturity curve.
You can set proxy targets for each education step and use them safely.
You can apply the kill and scale rules to funnels whose results arrive late.

steps.h: Why slow funnels need different timing
steps.p: Education funnels bring FTDs days or weeks after the click. Judge them on day 3 and you kill good funnels. Wait forever and you keep bad ones. The fix is to judge by cohort, know how mature each cohort is and use early signals carefully.

d.s: Judge cohorts when they are mature enough to judge.

steps.say: Education funnels bring F T Ds, first time deposits, days or weeks after the click. Judge them on day three and you kill good funnels. Wait forever and you keep bad ones. The fix is to judge by cohort, know how mature each cohort is, and use early signals carefully. As the slide says: same rules, better timing.

steps.p: Example. A weekly cohort from an education funnel, counted by days since click. By day 7, half of its eventual FTDs have arrived. By day 30, almost all. Your curve will differ; build it from your own data.
steps.say: This curve shows when F T Ds arrive, for an example weekly cohort, counted by days since click. Read along the bottom. By day seven, half of its eventual F T Ds have arrived. By day fourteen, about seventy two percent. By day thirty, almost all. Your curve will differ, so build it from your own data.

steps.p: Example built from the curve. Divide each day's cumulative FTDs by the day-45 total. This table tells you how much of a cohort's result you can see at each age.
steps.say: Here's a maturity table, built from that curve. Divide each day's cumulative F T Ds by the day forty five total, which is eighteen. Read down. Day three, five of eighteen, twenty eight percent. Day seven, nine of eighteen, fifty percent. Day fourteen, seventy two percent. Day thirty, ninety four percent. This table tells you how much of a cohort's result you can actually see at each age.

steps.h: Worked example: projecting a young cohort
steps.p: Example. A cohort is 7 days old and shows 6 FTDs on $400 of spend. At day 7 you usually see 50% of the final result, so the projected total is 12 FTDs and the projected CPA is about $33.
steps.more: Example maths: 6 ÷ 0.5 = 12. $400 ÷ 12 = $33.33 projected CPA. A projection is an estimate, not a result, and small numbers swing a lot: 6 FTDs could easily have been 4 or 8. Use projections to decide what to watch and when to hold, not to scale. Scaling waits for real, mature, qualified numbers.
steps.say: Now let's project a young cohort. It's seven days old, and shows six F T Ds on four hundred dollars of spend. At day seven, you usually see fifty percent of the final result. So read the sum on screen: six F T Ds divided by fifty percent equals twelve projected. That gives a projected C P A, cost per acquisition, of about thirty three dollars. But a projection is an estimate, not a result. Six could easily have been four or eight. Use projections to decide what to watch, not to scale.

steps.say: These mistakes are behind most wrong calls on education funnels. Read across. Counting F T Ds by deposit date: count by click or sign-up date. Scaling on a projection or a proxy: scale only on mature qualified F T Ds. Never updating the maturity curve: rebuild it monthly. Mixing funnels in one cohort table: one table per funnel and geo. steps.p: Starting rules to adapt. Proxies can kill or trigger a fix early; only mature, network-confirmed, qualified FTDs can scale. Write these into your plan before launch.

Kill at 2 × target CPA of matured spend with 0 FTDs

Proxy cost > 1.5 × proxy target after 50+ step events = kill or fix early

steps.say: Here are your starting rules for slow funnels. Matured spend means spend on cohorts at least thirty days old, adjusted to your curve. Kill at two times target C P A of matured spend with zero F T Ds. Kill if C P A is above the lower of one point five times target and break-even, after three times target matured spend. If a proxy cost is over one point five times its target after fifty or more step events, kill or fix early. Scale twenty percent every forty eight hours or more, only at mature C P A of point eight times target or better, with at least three qualified F T Ds. And rebuild your maturity curve monthly.

exam.why: Retention below 50% means fix first, and scaling needs ≥ 3 qualified FTDs.

exam.q: A presenter wants to show a live trade making money to 'prove it works'. What do you say?
options: No: live profit demonstrations are misleading; teach on a demo with risk
exam.why: Showing profits as proof is an income claim, whatever the disclaimer.

exam.q: A 7-day-old cohort shows 4 FTDs on $300. Your curve says day 7 is 50% mature. Target $40. What is the right call?
options: Hold and watch; projected CPA $37.50 is an estimate
exam.why: 4 ÷ 0.5 = 8 projected; $300 ÷ 8 = $37.50. A projection means watch, not scale.

Untick it and make the wording clear

exam.q: Your bot wants to message 5,000 people who joined last year but never started the bot. What is right?
options: Do not: bots cannot message people who never started them, apart from the join-request window
Send it from a second bot
Ask the network to send it
exam.why: Telegram bots can only message people who started them, except during the join-request window.
